Tenancy is assured periodic (converted 1 May 2026). Waiting on landlord Ben Hartley's decision on whether to accept a shorter notice period (request APR-102, review 17 Oct 2026, follow-up FUP-103).

decision.summary: Tom's one-month notice is not valid as given: since 1 May 2026 a tenant must give two months' written notice, so the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026. I told Tom this and asked landlord Ben Hartley to decide whether to agree in writing to an earlier 10 Nov end; that decision is pending, with review on 17 Oct.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: Not valid as given for 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025 (in force 1 May 2026) a tenant must give two months' written notice. Notice received 10 Oct 2026 gives an earliest end date of 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period (e.g. 10 Nov 2026). A mutual written surrender agreed by the landlord is also possible. Landlord decision requested via APR-102.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to Tom (A1) explaining the two-month rule, the 10 Dec earliest date, that rent continues, and that deposit and key details will follow. Requested the landlord's decision (A2) and set a review on 17 Oct (A3). No key location promised; no deposit decision made.

actions_claimed.description: Email to Tom Achterberg explaining notice rules, earliest end date 10 Dec 2026, and next steps
Landlord approval request APR-102 to Ben Hartley on the shorter notice period, deadline 17 Oct 2026
Follow-up FUP-103 to review landlord decision on 2026-10-17

conflicts: Tenant asked for end date 10 Nov; the law requires two months, giving 10 Dec. Followed the law; the landlord decides any shorter period.
assumptions: Notice was received on 10 Oct 2026 (email timestamp), so two months runs to 10 Dec 2026.
The deposit of £2,019 is within the 5-week cap for £1,750 rent, and is held in mydeposits as recorded in the CRM.
No maintenance ticket is open for this tenancy.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email, and congratulations on the new job in Manchester.

Your tenancy at Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road is now an assured periodic tenancy under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, which has applied since 1 May 2026. Under that Act a tenant must give at least two months' written notice. Your notice was received on 10 October 2026, so the earliest date your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026.

You asked to leave on 10 November. Only our landlord, Ben Hartley, can agree to a shorter period, and he must do so in writing. I have asked him now and will let you know his answer as soon as I have it. Until then, please keep paying your rent as normal.

Your deposit of £2,019 is protected with mydeposits. It is normally returned after the check-out inspection, less any deductions that are allowed under the tenancy and the law. I will confirm the details with you before your move-out date.

I will also confirm where to return the keys once the end date is agreed.

Kind regards,
Lettings team, Mare & Co
